div.head: Hn 58
div.ab: (C. LVIII) De homine uaganti. Aliter de uaganti si dominum habeat, aliter si non habeat: quod si fuerit et alicubi forisfaciat, ostendatur iusticie qu[i] preerit, et consilio eius agatur.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 577 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: wenn der Vagant herrenlos, wird er dem Gerichtsherrn des Thatorts vorgeführt; vgl. 82, 2
if the vagrant has no lord, he is brought before the lord holding jurisdiction over the place of the deed; cf. 82, 2
Vgl. Gl Gefolge 9k—uago{16}—que{18} original (da iusticia, auch trotz Bed. ‘Richter’, als Fem. oft im Normann. Latein vorkommt; z. B. Urk. [1120—28] Cunnigham Growth Engl. industry 541) Rs
Cf. Gl Gefolge 9k—uago{16}—que{18} original (since iusticia, even with the meaning ‘judge’, often occurs as a feminine in Norman Latin; e.g. charter [1120—28] Cunnigham Growth Engl. industry 541) Rs

div.ab: (Ch. LVIII) Concerning a vagrant man. [It is] one way with a vagrant if he has a lord, another if he has not: and if there is such [a man] and he commits an offence anywhere, let him be shown to the justice who is in charge, and let the matter be dealt with by his counsel.
